pr_title: demo: quality review target — search with code smells

findings.title: Age filter silently rejects valid naive ISO timestamps
findings.explanation: The `age:` filter parses `created_at` for every matching token and compares it to an aware UTC `now`. If `created_at` is a valid ISO timestamp without timezone information, subtracting it from an aware datetime raises `TypeError`, which is swallowed and turns the note into a non-match. This can silently exclude valid notes depending on timestamp format.
findings.suggestion: Normalize timestamp handling explicitly: require timezone-aware `created_at` values, or treat naive timestamps as UTC with `created = created.replace(tzinfo=dt.UTC)`. Catch only expected parsing errors such as `ValueError`, not every exception.

findings.title: Unused imports are suppressed for hypothetical future use
findings.explanation: The module keeps unused `os` and `sys` imports with `noqa` comments saying they may be needed later. This suppresses linting for dead code and adds noise to a new module.
findings.suggestion: Remove unused imports until they are actually needed instead of suppressing Ruff diagnostics preemptively.

findings.title: Search function is overly complex and duplicates parsing logic
findings.explanation: `search` has high cyclomatic complexity and combines query parsing, per-token validation, date parsing, length comparison, and filtering in one nested loop. It also repeats similar `len:` parsing/comparison branches, making future query operators harder to add safely.
findings.suggestion: Parse the query once into small predicate functions or filter objects, and extract handlers for `text`, `tag`, `age`, and `len`. For `len`, parse the operator and threshold once, then dispatch via `operator.gt/lt/eq`.

findings.title: Broad exception handlers hide unexpected failures
findings.explanation: The code catches `Exception` for date and integer parsing. This hides unexpected programming errors, makes debugging harder, and can convert unrelated failures into simple non-matches.
findings.suggestion: Catch specific exceptions such as `ValueError` for `int()` and `datetime.fromisoformat()`, and avoid wrapping unrelated comparison logic in the same `try` block.

findings.title: Deduplication uses an inefficient and fragile JSON key list
findings.explanation: `dedup_results` stores serialized keys in a list, so membership checks are O(n) and the whole function is O(n²). `json.dumps([n.id, n.text])` is also an indirect way to build a deduplication key and may fail or behave unexpectedly if fields are not JSON-serializable.
findings.suggestion: Use a set of tuple keys, for example `seen: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()` and `key = (n.id, n.text)`, then check/add the key in O(1). If note IDs are unique, consider deduplicating by `n.id` alone.

summary: The main concern is a medium-severity quality issue where the age filter can silently reject valid naive ISO timestamps. Other findings are low-severity maintainability and robustness issues in search parsing, exception handling, imports, and deduplication.
